summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia status post allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was readmitted one day after discharge due to a new dry cough and malaise. He had no fever, shortness of breath, or signs of pneumonia on imaging. Labs showed stable mild acute kidney injury likely due to poor oral intake, slightly elevated liver enzymes consistent with known GVHD and congestive hepatopathy, and hyperuricemia managed with allopurinol. Viral studies were negative. His chronic heart failure regimen was maintained with torsemide, and all immunosuppressive and supportive therapies were continued. He improved symptomatically, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue medications, and follow up with outpatient providers for kidney and liver monitoring and potential initiation of an ACE inhibitor.
